Criteria text

Own simulation verification criteria — version 1

These are my claims about my simulation, not official success criteria or an official evaluation. They are fixed before building or evaluating a trained policy. Evidence is TASK.md and recorded reconstruction version6 (r0010), especially analysis/measurements.json, spin_and_hold_measurements.json, wrist_rate_feasibility.json, the video and comparison. A later change requires a recorded new version and reason; failure is not grounds to silently lower a threshold.

Measurement basis and ambiguities

The instruction orders: toss/catch; spin/toss/catch; spin/toss/catch; spin/hold. The human right hand stays palm up, dips and rises for launches, opens for flight and closes for catches. Release/catch transitions are uncertain by one30-fps frame at each boundary. The specified65mm ball is represented by one free physical sphere. Its orientation is unobservable as a globally calibrated quantity in the reconstruction. Incidental video seam/logo flow supports approximate local rotation; it is used to define meaningful roll/spin amounts, never treated as exact measured quaternions.

The brief second spin is a partial roll, not evidence for a whole revolution. The two long spin intervals show substantial rolling with changes of axis/direction; no fixed spin axis or monotonic complete revolution is required. Small orientation fidget in the final hold is allowed. The final hold may be extended after the video ends. Absolute camera depth is uncertain; wrist comparison uses one fixed, documented anatomical retargeting, constant yaw and translation chosen before evaluation. No per-episode time warping or fitted pose alignment is allowed.

Episode and event definitions

The simulation record defines an initial settling period; the skill clock starts immediately after it. The nominal reference lasts10.4667s. An episode must finish by skill time11.5s, allowing roughly1s for a longer final retention and actuator/contact transitions. All object motion comes from dynamics and physical contact; no object pose resets, attachments, external ball forces or scripted object motion are allowed during the skill.

A flight is a maximal no-hand-contact interval, ignoring gaps shorter than20ms when counting substantial events. A qualifying toss must have a true release with positive vertical velocity and pass criterion2 below. A catch starts at first hand contact following a qualifying flight. A retained interval means the ball centre is within0.16m of the wrist and is supported by physical hand contact. The reference held distance is mostly0.08–0.13m; the additional3cm allows the different hand geometry and contact-location uncertainty while excluding distant balancing tricks.

For spin, let Qrel(t)=R_wrist(t)^T R_ball(t). Angular travel is the sum of shortest rotation magnitudes between successive Qrel states over retained frames; maximum excursion is the maximum geodesic angle from the spin interval's initial Qrel. Compute at500Hz. Count only retained motion; a detached ball spinning in flight cannot satisfy an in-hand spin. Excursion requirements prevent tiny high-frequency vibration from satisfying a path-length requirement.

Per-episode requirements (all, in this order)

  1. Start retained. After settling, the ball is in physical hand contact, within0.16m of the wrist, with finite bounded states. No ball-floor contact occurs at any point in the skill. The video shows no environmental contact.
  1. Exactly three substantial tosses and catches. Each toss has a continuous no-hand-contact flight lasting0.40–0.60s, release-to-apex vertical rise0.25–0.38m, and horizontal release-to-catch displacement≤0.08m. Its mean free-flight vertical acceleration must be within1.0m/s² of−9.81. The measured durations are0.467–0.500s; two boundary frames span0.067s. The lower height allows roughlyone ball radius below the smallest measured rise; the upper height includes abouttwo radii above the largest, covering uncertain release instant and different finger release geometry. Horizontal tolerance adds roughlyone diameter to the measured2–3cm drift, preserving a nearly vertical toss. Flight contact absence plus gravity prevents counting a carried ball as a toss.

Releases occur within±0.20s of1.7333,5.4333,6.6667s. This includes33ms video uncertainty, roughly0.1s for an0.8rad finger change at the specified8rad/s MCP speed, and contact/target settling. It preserves the demonstrated rhythm. Each catch must retain the ball for≥0.20s before a subsequent substantial release. The corresponding video capture intervals last0.333–0.567s; the tolerance covers two uncertain frames and different robot contact timing. No additional qualifying toss is allowed.

  1. Ordered in-hand spins. Between the first catch and second toss, angular travel≥2πrad and maximum excursion≥2.0rad. Between the second catch and third toss, angular travel≥0.8rad and maximum excursion≥0.5rad. After the third catch and before final hold, angular travel≥2πrad and maximum excursion≥2.0rad. The measured long travels8.745/8.261rad and excursions3.141/2.766rad exceed these thresholds; the shorter measured travel1.371rad and excursion0.738rad support a partial roll. Margins account for texture/depth/wrist fitting error and the residual angular fidget measured during the hold; they do not redefine the short roll as a full turn. At least80% of each spin interval must be retained, with thumb/opposing-finger contact or palm-plus-finger support. The reconstructed opposed-contact fractions are95.2–100%; the tolerance allows rolling contact changes and different fingertip geometry.
  1. Human-like wrist and finger motion. Against the fixed retargeted anatomical reference at the same skill time: wrist-position RMS error≤0.05m and maximum error≤0.10m; wrist-orientation geodesic RMS error≤15deg and maximum≤35deg. Evaluate from skill start through the nominal video end. Position tolerances cover correlated monocular depth uncertainty and different hand scale/contact placement while staying well below the demonstrated11–16cm launch excursion. Orientation tolerances combine the measured16.75deg peak target-rate deviation, approximately8deg fit/prior discrepancy, and contact adaptation; the small2.35deg RMS rate deviation leaves most of the15deg RMS allowance for those uncertainties. At least95% of retained samples have palm-normal tilt≤60deg from up; the demonstrated phase medians are18–48deg. For at leastthree long fingers, the mean (MCP_flex+PIP+DIP)/3 flexion in the0.15s after each catch exceeds its mean in the middle0.15s of the preceding flight by≥0.20rad. The observed human bend contrast is roughly0.3–0.5rad; this verifies an open/catch transition with allowance for different joints.
  1. Final secure hold. A final continuous retained interval≥0.40s, with no substantial release, follows the last spin. During it, wrist-relative ball-centre drift from the interval start≤0.015m, relative angular excursion≤0.30rad, and palm tilt≤60deg. The video hold is0.433s with7.69mm centre drift and0.205rad angular excursion. About7mm extra position tolerance covers contact compliance, shape mismatch and reconstruction noise;0.095rad angular tolerance covers texture/wrist fitting uncertainty. At leasttwo distinct hand links support/retain the ball for≥80% of the interval.
  1. Hardware and learning validity. At every physics tick, all20 finger positions stay within URDF limits±0.02rad, speeds stay within their exact limits, applied torques stay within effort limits, and all actions are finite and correctly shaped. Wrist/finger controllers, noise, update rates and target limits match hardware/SPECS.md. Any finger violation makes the episode fail. The verified actor uses only permitted deployable observations and outputs through those controllers. Its network has been trained with PPO. Baseline/reference-only performance must be reported separately; a scripted success is not evidence of learned PPO success.

Aggregate verdict and evidence

Use20 fixed evaluation seeds1000–1019, with initial wrist translation independently uniform±2mm per axis, finger angles independently uniform±0.01rad clipped to limits, and ball-centre translation independently uniform±1mm per axis. These small perturbations are below the demonstrated motion/shape uncertainty and test local closed-loop robustness without changing the task. Physics is the recorded nominal simulation unless a separately labeled robustness test is added. Encoder noise remains active. A passing verdict requires at least18/20 episodes to meet all per-episode criteria and zero hardware violations in all20. This90% aggregate threshold is an explicit research reliability assumption, not a statistic measured from the single video. Report the count, every per-criterion metric, failure seeds, checkpoint, simulation and criteria versions, raw trajectories and top/left/right videos of a passing and a failing episode when one exists. A single attractive rollout is insufficient.

Limitations remain: simulation contact/material approximations, monocular human-pose ambiguity, incomplete visual spin evidence and ideal object-state observations. Passing these criteria would establish only my own result in the recorded simulation.
